items.title: CVE-2026-33824 (CVSS 9.8): Microsoft IKE Double-Free RCE Actively Exploited by Chinese-Nexus Threat Actor
items.summary: A double-free vulnerability in Microsoft Internet Key Exchange (IKE) Service Extensions allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code over the network. Being actively exploited in the wild by a Chinese-speaking threat actor. Patched in August 2026 Patch Tuesday alongside 420 other CVEs; affects all Windows deployments using IKE for VPN/IPsec.
items.why: CVSS 9.8 with confirmed state-actor exploitation against VPN perimeter infrastructure. A pre-auth RCE on IKE means attackers can gain footholds before any endpoint visibility fires. Patch immediately and hunt for lateral movement from perimeter VPN endpoints.
items.source: The Hacker News / Microsoft August 2026 Patch Tuesday

items.title: CVE-2026-69836 (CVSS 10.0): Microsoft Entra ID Deserialization Flaw Enables Unauthenticated RCE
items.summary: A maximum-severity deserialization vulnerability in Microsoft Entra ID allows unauthenticated remote code execution against the cloud identity platform. Disclosed and patched in August 2026 Patch Tuesday. Affects all organizations using Entra ID for Microsoft 365 and Azure identity management.
items.why: CVSS 10.0 on the IAM backbone of millions of organizations. Unauthenticated RCE on Entra ID enables token forgery, cross-tenant pivoting, and full Azure tenancy takeover. Treat as absolute critical-priority patch — no mitigating controls compensate for an identity-layer RCE.
items.source: Hoplon InfoSec / Microsoft August 2026 Patch Tuesday

items.title: APT42 Supercharges SpearSpecter Campaign with Generative AI: Multilingual Lures, AI Personas, Fileless TAMECAT Backdoor
items.summary: Iran-linked APT42 has integrated generative AI across its full SpearSpecter attack chain — target profiling, multilingual phishing lures, persona creation, and malware development — and deploys an upgraded fileless TAMECAT backdoor via legitimate cloud C2. Targets include governments, defence contractors, think tanks, and nuclear-sector entities.
items.why: AI-generated phishing strips the grammatical and cultural tells that previously exposed state-sponsored campaigns, dramatically increasing success rates. Fileless TAMECAT leaves minimal forensic artifacts, and cloud-service C2 blends into normal traffic. Defenders must shift to behavioral and cloud-access anomaly detection — signature-based controls will not catch this.
items.source: Malware Patrol Late-August 2026 Threat Reports / Tata Communications Threat Advisory

items.title: ChainDrop npm Supply Chain Attack: 400+ Packages, 2,000 Versions Poisoned; Persists via VS Code and Claude Code Config Hijack
items.summary: ChainDrop compromised 400+ unrelated npm packages across 2,000 versions by hijacking a single maintainer account. The malware steals credentials, establishes persistence by modifying VS Code and Claude Code configuration files, and republishes poisoned packages to propagate infections downstream. Every developer machine that ran npm install of any affected version is silently compromised.
items.why: Massive npm blast radius with a novel persistence vector abusing IDE config files (VS Code, Claude Code) to survive reinstalls. Any developer system that consumed an affected package warrants full credential rotation and incident response — not just a package update.

items.title: Mandiant M-Trends 2026: PROMPTFLUX & PROMPTSTEAL — Malware Querying LLMs Mid-Execution to Dynamically Evade Detection
items.summary: Mandiant's M-Trends 2026 report (500,000+ hours of IR investigations) documents PROMPTFLUX and PROMPTSTEAL — novel malware families that query large language models at runtime to generate evasion logic on the fly, defeating static signatures and heuristics. The report also documents 'distillation attacks' that steal proprietary ML model logic from enterprise APIs as IP theft.
items.why: First confirmed in-the-wild use of LLMs as live evasion engines inside malware. Runtime-generated evasion invalidates static signatures and most heuristics — defenders urgently need behavioral telemetry and AI-vs-AI detection. This is the transition to adaptive malware the industry has warned about.
